bibl.title: Automatic Chemical Design Using a Data-Driven Continuous Representation of Molecules

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Chemical space, and how to search it by turning molecules into vectors that can be optimised with gradients.
span.quote: To solve the inverse design challenge in chemistry, we convert molecules into continuous vector representations using neural networks.

span.label: Molecular space is discrete and unstructured, so gradients cannot guide a search through it - can it be made continuous instead?
span.quote: Discrete optimization methods have difficulty effectively searching large areas of chemical space because it is not possible to guide the search with gradients.

span.label: An encoder/decoder/predictor trained jointly, so that molecules become points in a continuous space where optimisation and interpolation are ordinary operations.
span.quote: Continuous representations of molecules allow us to automatically generate novel chemical structures by performing simple operations in the latent space, such as decoding random vectors, perturbing known chemical structures, or interpolating between molecules.

span.label: method
span.quote: We report a method to convert discrete representations of molecules to and from a multidimensional continuous representation.

span.label: automated molecular design in chemical space
span.quote: The goal of drug and material design is to identify novel molecules that have certain desirable properties.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: A deep neural network was trained on hundreds of thousands of existing chemical structures to construct three coupled functions: an encoder, a decoder, and a predictor.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: encoding molecules into a continuous latent space so new molecules are generated by decoding/interpolating vectors (and properties optimized by moving in that space)
span.quote: by performing simple operations in the latent space, such as decoding random vectors

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: an information bottleneck forces the network to keep only what is statistically salient - the compression is what makes the vector a representation rather than a copy
span.quote: This bottleneck—here the fixed-length continuous vector—induces the network to learn a compressed representation that captures the most statistically salient information in the data.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the variational penalty fills in the space: adding noise to the encoding forces the decoder to handle points between molecules, so the space has no dead areas
span.quote: The intuition is that adding noise to the encoded molecules forces the decoder to learn how to decode a wider variety of latent points and find more robust representations.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: training the property predictor JOINTLY is what aligns the geometry with the chemistry - otherwise moving in the space would not move the property
span.quote: Second, if we develop a differentiable model that maps from molecular representations to desirable properties, we can enable the use of gradient-based optimization to make larger jumps in chemical space.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: invalid outputs are filtered rather than prevented - the decoder is allowed to be wrong and a cheminformatics toolkit discards the failures
span.quote: We employed the open source cheminformatics suite RDKit 30 to validate the chemical structures of output molecules and discard invalid ones.

span.label: optimization in molecular space is hard because the search space is large, discrete, and unstructured
span.note: what this limits: any claim of coverage over chemical space: OPTIMIZATION IN MOLECULAR SPACE IS EXTREMELY CHALLENGING, BECAUSE THE SEARCH SPACE IS LARGE, DISCRETE, AND UNSTRUCTURED
span.quote: optimization in molecular space is extremely challenging, because the search space is large, discrete, and unstructured

span.label: Decoded molecules can be graph-valid but chemically undesirable.
span.note: what this limits: the generated molecules: THE AUTOENCODER SOMETIMES PRODUCED MOLECULES THAT ARE FORMALLY VALID AS GRAPHS BUT CONTAIN MOIETIES THAT ARE NOT DESIRABLE BECAUSE OF STABILITY OR SYNTHETIC CONSTRAINTS
span.quote: The autoencoder sometimes produced molecules that are formally valid as graphs but contain moieties that are not desirable because of stability or synthetic constraints.

span.label: SMILES syntax fragility means the decoder still emits invalid molecules despite the variational constraint.
span.note: what this limits: the decoder's output: THE CHARACTER-BY-CHARACTER NATURE OF THE SMILES REPRESENTATION AND THE FRAGILITY OF ITS INTERNAL SYNTAX CAN STILL RESULT IN THE OUTPUT OF INVALID strings
span.quote: The character-by-character nature of the SMILES representation and the fragility of its internal syntax (opening and closing cycles and branches, allowed valences, etc.) can still result in the output of invalid molecules from the decoder, even with the variational constraint.

span.label: Requiring the decoder to learn SMILES validity makes the learning problem harder than it needs to be.
span.note: what this limits: the learning problem as posed: FORCING THE DECODER TO PRODUCE VALID SMILES STRINGS MAKES THE LEARNING PROBLEM UNNECESSARILY HARD SINCE THE DECODER MUST ALSO IMPLICITLY LEARN WHICH STRINGS ARE VALID SMILES
span.quote: Forcing the decoder to produce valid SMILES strings makes the learning problem unnecessarily hard since the decoder must also implicitly learn which strings are valid SMILES.

span.label: Decoding succeeds only near known molecules; random latent points almost always fail.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about generating novel molecules: THE PROBABILITY OF DECODING FROM A POINT IN LATENT SPACE IS DEPENDENT ON HOW CLOSE THIS POINT IS TO THE LATENT REPRESENTATIONS OF OTHER MOLECULES - a decoding rate of 73-79% NEAR known molecules
span.quote: The probability of decoding from a point in latent space is dependent on how close this point is to the latent representations of other molecules; we observed a decoding rate of 73–79% for points that are close to known molecules, and 4% for randomly selected latent points.

span.label: Property-prediction accuracy is only comparable to graph convolutions for some properties and is not fully optimised.
span.note: what this limits: the property-prediction comparison: PERFORMANCE FOR ELECTRONIC PROPERTIES ARE SIMILAR TO GRAPH CONVOLUTIONS FOR SOME PROPERTIES, and accuracy COULD BE IMPROVED
span.quote: Our VAE model shows that property prediction performance for electronic properties (i.e., orbital energies) are similar to graph convolutions for some properties; prediction accuracy could be improved with further hyperparameter optimization.

span.label: The graph-output alternative the authors prefer is not yet solvable.
span.note: what this limits: the graph-output alternative the authors prefer: BUILDING A NEURAL NETWORK WHICH CAN OUTPUT ARBITRARY GRAPHS IS AN OPEN PROBLEM
span.quote: However, building a neural network which can output arbitrary graphs is an open problem.

span.label: The decoder still emits chemically invalid strings, because SMILES syntax is fragile and the model works character by character.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - SMILES syntax fragility still yields invalid output
span.quote: The character-by-character nature of the SMILES representation and the fragility of its internal syntax (opening and closing cycles and branches, allowed valences, etc.) can still result in the output of invalid molecules from the decoder, even with the variational constraint.

span.label: Without the variational constraint the latent space contains dead regions that decode to nothing valid.
span.note: what this limits: the latent space without the variational constraint: IT MAY BE SPARSE AND MAY CONTAIN LARGE DEAD AREAS, WHICH DECODE TO INVALID SMILES STRINGS
span.quote: Without this constraint, the latent space learned by the autoencoder may be sparse and may contain large “dead areas”, which decode to invalid SMILES strings.

span.label: The choice of string encoding is load-bearing and only partly explained - InChI performed substantially worse and the reason is offered as a presumption.
span.note: what this limits: every result in the paper, which is conditional on the encoding: WE ALSO TESTED InChI AS AN ALTERNATIVE STRING REPRESENTATION, BUT FOUND IT TO PERFORM SUBSTANTIALLY WORSE THAN SMILES, PRESUMABLY DUE TO A MORE COMPLEX SYNTAX THAT INCLUDES COUNTING AND ARITHMETIC
span.quote: We also tested InChI 29 as an alternative string representation, but found it to perform substantially worse than SMILES, presumably due to a more complex syntax that includes counting and arithmetic.

span.label: a variational autoencoder mapping molecules (SMILES strings) into a continuous latent space for automatic chemical design
span.quote: We apply such generative models to chemical design, using a pair of deep networks trained as an autoencoder to convert molecules represented as SMILES strings into a continuous vector representation

span.label: the variational autoencoder with recurrent encoder and decoder, taken from Bowman et al.'s work on English sentences and applied to molecules as strings
span.quote: Variational autoencoders with recurrent neural network encoding/decoding were proposed by Bowman et al. in the context of written English sentences, and we followed their approach closely. 20

span.label: the idea that a low-dimensional continuous code supports interpolation and analogy, imported as the reason a molecular latent space should be navigable
span.quote: Such models usually also produce low-dimensional continuous representations of the data being modeled, allowing interpolation or analogical reasoning for natural images, 19 text, 20 speech, and music. 21 , 22

span.label: only CANONICALISED SMILES strings used for training
span.quote: We used only canonicalized SMILES for training to avoid dealing with equivalent SMILES representations.

span.label: variational autoencoder
span.quote: VAEs generalize autoencoders, adding stochasticity to the encoder which combined with a penalty term encourages all areas of the latent space to correspond to a valid decoding.

span.label: latent representation
span.quote: We call the vector-encoded molecule the latent representation of the molecule.

span.label: SMILES
span.quote: We chose to use SMILES representation because this representation can be readily converted into a molecule.

span.label: InChI
span.quote: We also tested InChI 29 as an alternative string representation, but found it to perform substantially worse than SMILES, presumably due to a more complex syntax that includes counting and arithmetic.

span.label: autoencoder
span.quote: Key to the design of the autoencoder is the mapping of strings through an information bottleneck .

span.label: information bottleneck
span.quote: This bottleneck—here the fixed-length continuous vector—induces the network to learn a compressed representation that captures the most statistically salient information in the data.

span.label: chemical space
span.quote: However, optimization in molecular space is extremely challenging, because the search space is large, discrete, and unstructured.

span.label: gradient-based optimization
span.quote: Second, if we develop a differentiable model that maps from molecular representations to desirable properties, we can enable the use of gradient-based optimization to make larger jumps in chemical space.

span.label: representation - DISCRETE: the molecule as a symbol string, which a chemist can read and a machine can turn back into a structure
span.quote: We chose to use SMILES representation because this representation can be readily converted into a molecule.

span.label: representation - CONTINUOUS: the molecule as a real-valued vector, on which arithmetic and gradients are defined
span.quote: We report a method to convert discrete representations of molecules to and from a multidimensional continuous representation.

span.label: representation - LATENT: specifically the compressed code inside the bottleneck, which is a representation because it discards, not because it depicts
span.quote: This bottleneck—here the fixed-length continuous vector—induces the network to learn a compressed representation that captures the most statistically salient information in the data.

span.label: representation - as used across images, text, speech and music, where the same low-dimensional continuous code supports interpolation and analogy
span.quote: Such models usually also produce low-dimensional continuous representations of the data being modeled, allowing interpolation or analogical reasoning for natural images, 19 text, 20 speech, and music. 21 , 22

span.note: RETRACTED: THE PAPER'S OWN WORD AND THE FIELD'S TAXONOMY POINT OPPOSITE WAYS, AND I WILL NOT DECIDE IT FOR THEM. The edge says `autoencoder --is-a--> variational autoencoder`. Its span is 'VAEs GENERALIZE autoencoders, ADDING STOCHASTICITY to the encoder'. Read on `generalize`, a VAE is the broader class and the edge is right. Read on `adding`, a VAE is an autoencoder PLUS machinery - a SPECIALISATION - and the edge is backwards, which is also how the field standardly uses the terms. Replacing it would mean overriding the paper's own verb with my knowledge of the taxonomy; leaving it asserts a reading the sentence does not settle. WITHDRAWN, with the ambiguity recorded, which is the only move that adds no claim the text does not make. — strength of the relation: 1 — the paper says VAEs GENERALIZE autoencoders, so the plain autoencoder is the special case and the arrow runs that way. Same reading applied to 'SIS is a generalization of the contact process' in pastorsatorras2001.
